newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Thousands wait for Kabila in Kinshasa.
newsitem.headline: Thousands wait for Kabila in Kinshasa.

text.p: Tens of thousands of residents of the Zaire capital walked to the airport on Tuesday hoping to catch a first glimpse of self-proclaimed president Laurent Kabila but were turned back by rebel troops, witnesses said.
Crowds started surging towards the airport on the eastern outskirts of the city of five million people following rumours that Kabila was due to fly in from southern Lubumbashi.
Kabila's rebel soldiers, who captured Kinshasa at the weekend after a seven-month guerrilla advance from the eastern border with Rwanda, blocked the way near the airport.

South Africa, which mediated between Kabila and ousted dictator Mobutu Sese Seko, announced on Monday that Kabila would arrive in Kinshasa on Tuesday to unveil a new government for the renamed Democratic Republic of Congo.
The independent Kinshasa daily Reference Plus on Tuesday reproduced the South African announcement on its front page.
But a top Kabila aide said his leader would not arrive in Kinshasa as expected. Security adviser Paul Kabongo told Reuters in Kinshasa that Kabila would come at an "opportune time."
However, another senior rebel alliance official, who declined to be named, said Kabila would fly to Kinshasa on Tuesday though it was not being announced in advance for security reasons.
